content:
Hi! This is my first time asking on zulip. So apologies if there's anything inappropriate.

Currently (by 2026-09-30T21:00:00+08:00) add_div requires DivisionSemiring K, but DivInvMonoid K + Distrib K should be enough? I'm relatively new to Lean/Mathlib, please correct me if I misunderstood.

Q1. Is this expected?

I can write div_eq_mul_inv and add_mul to prove the goal.

Also I noticed that ENNReal implemented a separate add_div, maybe that is another example related.

Q2. How can I help to improve this if current state is not desirable?

I ran into this when writing something related to Positive, I understand this might be only a tip of the iceberg. Maybe the better approach is to re-organize the theorems around Algebra/Order/Positive and Algebra/Field to use the weakest typeclass possible? If this is a problem needs to be solved, I'm glad to help (e.g. opening an issue/make a draft PR?).

it looks like DivInvMonoid and Distrib both contain the data of a multiplication, so inside the proof you would have two multiplications, one from the DivInvMonoid which plays nice with division and one from the Distrib which plays nice with addition, and no way to relate them

Thanks for the reply! I understand this now.
So adding Positive.add_div is a possible solution? Is there any plan or issue template-ish stuff I should look into?

docs#Finset.sum_div is another example which requires DivisionSemiring but doesn't need its full power (see #40855).
The solution is to introduce a new typeclass, e.g. in your case class DistribDivInvMonoid K extends Distrib K, DivInvMonoid K, but you'd have to find a bunch more lemmas to motivate such a class.
